He played [[college basketball]] for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]] and [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn Tigers]]. ==Early life== Kessler played basketball for [[Woodward Academy]] in [[College Park, Georgia]]. In his senior season, he averaged 17.8 points, 9.3 rebounds and 5.2 blocks per game, leading his team to its first Class 4A state title. During his time at Woodward, he played on the varsity basketball team with [[Golden State Warriors]] guard, [[Will Richard]], who was also on the 2020 state championship team. Kessler was named ''[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]'' Player of the Year, [[Mr. Georgia Basketball]] and Georgia [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]].{{cite web |last1=Holcomb |first1=Todd |title=7-foot Walker Kessler is Georgia's boys basketball player of the year |url=https://www.ajc.com/blog/high-school-sports/foot-walker-kessler-georgia-boys-basketball-player-the-year/HXxn1BTby550avlPFRmiMO/ |website=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] |access-date=April 12, 2021 |date=March 26, 2020}}{{cite web |last1=Smith |first1=Adam |title=New UNC coach Hubert Davis's pursuit comes up empty as transfer Walker Kessler picks Auburn |url=https://www.thetimesnews.com/story/sports/college/acc/2021/04/13/unc-basketball-pursuit-comes-up-empty-walker-kessler-picks-auburn/7200236002/ |website=[[Times-News (Burlington, North Carolina)|Times-News]] |access-date=April 13, 2021 |date=April 13, 2021}} He was a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] selection.{{cite web |last1=Green |first1=Tom |title=A closer look at Walker Kessler and Auburn basketball's retooled roster (so far) |url=https://www.al.com/auburnbasketball/2021/04/a-closer-look-at-walker-kessler-and-auburn-basketballs-retooled-roster-so-far.html |website=AL.com |access-date=April 13, 2021 |date=April 13, 2021}} Kessler competed for Game Elite on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] circuit.{{cite web |last1=Jordan |first1=Jason |title=adidas Gauntlet: Elite 2020 center Walker Kessler is wide open despite deep family ties to Georgia |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2019/adidas-gauntlet-elite-2020-center-walker-kessler-is-wide-open-despite-deep-family-ties-to-georgia |website=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=April 13, 2021 |date=April 13, 2019}} His jersey hangs outside of the varsity gym at Woodward Academy. A consensus five-star recruit and one of the top [[center (basketball)|centers]] in the 2020 class, he committed to playing college basketball for [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] over offers from [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]], [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]] and [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]], among others.{{cite magazine |last1=Carroll |first1=Charlotte |title=Five-star Center Walker Kessler Commits to North Carolina = yes }} ==College career== === North Carolina (2020–2021) === On March 10, 2021, Kessler posted 16 points, 12 rebounds and eight blocks in a 101–59 win over [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]] in the second round of the [[2021 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]]. He set a North Carolina freshman record and an ACC Tournament record for blocks in a game.{{cite web |title=Bacot, UNC beat Notre Dame 101–59, advance to ACC quarters |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2021/03/10/bacot-unc-beat-notre-dame-101-59-advance-to-acc-semis/43459333/ |website=[[USA Today]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=April 13, 2021 |date=March 10, 2021}} As a freshman, he averaged 4.4 points and 3.2 rebounds per game. === Auburn (2021–2022) === Following the season, Kessler transferred to [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], choosing the Tigers over [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]].{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Sought-after center Walker Kessler, one of the top players in the men's basketball transfer portal, commits to Auburn Tigers |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31245075/sought-center-walker-kessler-one-top-players-men-basketball-transfer-portal-commits-auburn-tigers |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=April 13, 2021 |date=April 12, 2021}} On December 29, 2021, he posted a [[triple-double]] of 16 points, a career-high 11 blocks and 10 rebounds against [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU]].{{cite news |last1=Wilborn |first1=Nubyjas |title=Walker Kessler gets triple-double in Auburn's 70–55 win and other thoughts from Auburn Arena |url=https://www.al.com/auburnbasketball/2021/12/walker-kessler-gets-triple-double-in-auburns-70-55-win-and-other-thoughts-from-auburn-arena.html |access-date=December 30, 2021 |work=[[Al.com]] |date=December 29, 2021}} On January 25, Kessler received SEC Player of the Week honors following strong performances against [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]] and [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]].{{Cite web|url=https://auburnwire.usatoday.com/2022/01/25/jabari-smith-walker-kessler-earn-sec-honors/|title=Jabari Smith, Walker Kessler earn SEC Honors|date=25 January 2022}} Kessler was regarded as one of the nations premier shot blockers, setting the Auburn single season block record, leading the nation in blocks and recording more blocks than all but 13 teams.{{Cite web|url=https://flywareagle.com/2022/02/17/auburn-basketball-kessler-blocks-stat/|title = Auburn basketball: This Walker Kessler blocks stat is ridiculous|date = 17 February 2022}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.al.com/auburnbasketball/2022/02/walker-kessler-breaks-auburns-single-season-blocks-record.html|title = Walker Kessler breaks Auburn single-season blocks record in win vs. Ole Miss|date = 24 February 2022}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Kessler was named the SEC Defensive Player of the Year, a member of the All-SEC First Team and a [[2022 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|3rd Team All American]].{{cite web | url=https://247sports.com/college/auburn/Article/Auburns-Walker-Kessler-SEC-Basketball-Defensive-Player-of-the-Year-184036415/ | title=Walker Kessler SEC Basketball Defensive Player of the Year }}{{cite web | url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-wisconsin-indiana-georgia-basketball-cffd2113c69053c28aa220a71ca94d69 | title=The Associated Press Men's All-America Teams | website=[[Associated Press]] | date=15 March 2022 }} On April 3, 2022, Kessler declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web|title=Auburn Tigers star big man Walker Kessler to enter NBA draft|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33664123/auburn-tigers-star-big-man-walker-kessler-enter-nba-draft|first=Jonathan|last=Givony|date=April 3, 2022|accessdate=April 3, 2022}} ==Professional career== === Utah Jazz (2022–2026) === Kessler was selected by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] with the 22nd overall pick before being traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], alongside [[TyTy Washington]], for [[Jake LaRavia]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-acquire-draft-rights-to-center-walker-kessler-from-memphis-grizzlies|title = Timberwolves Acquire Draft Rights to Center Walker Kessler from Memphis Grizzlies |website = [[NBA.com]] |date = June 24, 2022|accessdate=June 28, 2022}} On July 6, 2022, two weeks after being drafted, Kessler was traded along with [[Patrick Beverley]], [[Jarred Vanderbilt]], [[Leandro Bolmaro]], [[Malik Beasley]], four future first-round picks, and a pick swap to the [[Utah Jazz]] in exchange for [[Rudy Gobert]].{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Timberwolves Acquire Center Rudy Gobert from Utah Jazz |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/minnesota-timberwolves-acquire-center-rudy-gobert-from-utah-jazz |access-date=2022-07-06 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}} On July 9, Kessler signed his rookie scale contract with the Jazz.{{Cite web |title=Utah Jazz Sign Walker Kessler |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-walker-kessler |access-date=2022-07-14 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}} On January 16, 2023, Kessler put up a double-double with a career-high 20 points and a then career-high 21 rebounds, alongside four assists and two blocks in a 126–125 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web|url=https://www.al.com/sports/2023/01/walker-kessler-turns-in-2020-game-for-utah-jazz.html|title=Walker Kessler turns in 20/20 game for Utah Jazz|website=al.com|last=Inabinett|first=Mark|date=January 16, 2023|access-date=January 16, 2023}} On March 25, 2023, Kessler scored a career-high 31 points to go along with 11 rebounds in a 121–113 loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web | url=https://www.nba.com/game/uta-vs-sac-0022201111/box-score | title=Utah Jazz vs Sacramento Kings Mar 25, 2023 Box Scores | website=[[NBA.com]] }} Over the course of his rookie season he appeared in 74 games while averaging 9.2 points per game.{{Cite web |title=Walker Kessler Career Stats - NBA |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/stats/_/id/4433136/walker-kessler |access-date=2023-12-21 |website=ESPN |language=en}} At the conclusion of the 2022–23 season, Kessler was announced as a finalist for the [[NBA Rookie of the Year Award]], ultimately finishing third in the voting.{{cite web|url=https://www.slcdunk.com/2023/4/25/23698682/walker-kessler-takes-third-in-rookie-of-the-year-voting-paolo-banchero|title=Walker Kessler takes third in Rookie of the Year voting|website=slcdunk.com|last=Hansen|first=James|date=April 26, 2023|access-date=April 29, 2023}} Kessler made five starts for Utah during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], averaging 14.4 points, 10.8 rebounds, and 3.0 assists. On November 5, 2025, it was announced that Kessler would require season-ending left [[shoulder]] surgery to repair a torn labrum.{{cite web | title=Jazz starting big man to undergo season-ending surgery | website=basketnews.com | date=2025-11-05 | url=https://basketnews.com/news-234430-jazz-starting-big-man-to-undergo-season-ending-surgery.html | access-date=2025-12-06}} During his third year in [[Utah]], and already an undisputed starter, on March 7, 2025, he achieved a career-high 25 rebounds against the [[Toronto Raptors]], in addition to 18 points and a career-high eight blocks.{{Cite web |last=Press |first=The Associated |date=2025-03-08 |title=Quickley's 34 points overcome Kessler's 25 boards in Raptors' win over Jazz |url=https://thescore.com/nba/news/3236204 |access-date=2026-03-12 |website=theScore.com |language=en}} === Los Angeles Lakers (2026–present) === On July 8, 2026, Kessler signed a 4-year, $130 million contract with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] via a sign-and-trade with the Jazz in exchange for two first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps.{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Lakers Acquire Center Walker Kessler |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/lakers-acquire-center-walker-kessler |access-date=2026-07-08 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}} ==National team career== Kessler played for the [[2023 United States FIBA Basketball World Cup team|United States national team]] during the [[2023 FIBA World Cup]]. For the tournament, he averaged 4.0 points, 2.3 rebounds, and 1.3 blocks while helping the team secure a fourth-place finish.{{Cite web |title=Walker Kessler
